correctness.rationale: The exact conditional two-particle stationary weights obey detailed balance on every original graph transition. For the stationary centered collision indicator the reversible Green/Poisson variational identity is exact. After the rescaling z=a h, fast collision/adjacency edges have conductance of order 1/a, and separated-state moves have order-one conductance. The connected incidence subgraph forces the limiting fast coordinates to zero; uniform finite-dimensional coercivity and matching variational upper/lower bounds leave precisely the Dirichlet killed-nonedge walk. Its inverse gives expected adjacency hitting times. On complete graphs the indicator is lumpable into a two-state chain. On cycles the labeled relative walk and a solved hitting-time recurrence give the rational formula and derivative sign. The packaged exact-rational checker passed 42 full-state comparisons and small-diffusion tests. Limits are taken in the prescribed order; finite tests do not replace general proof.

value.rationale: The stationary collision variance has the same graph-independent O(a) decay on every connected graph, but its *time-integrated* covariance has a strictly positive finite limit exactly for noncomplete graphs. This gives a natural, sharp graph-topology test for metastable low-frequency collision noise and an explicit killed-walk hitting-time representation of its coefficient. The cycle rational formula quantifies the effect at all diffusivities and reveals a genuine size-three versus size-four monotonicity boundary. These are observable-specific transport-fluctuation structural results, not an arbitrary tiny finite-table computation or a restatement of the stationary measure.
